summary: In Greek mythology, Caeneus (Ancient Greek Καινεύς) son of Coronus is an Argonaut from Gortyn in Crete — listed by Hyginus and counted by Apollodorus separately from Coronus son of the Lapith Caeneus. He is not the invulnerable Lapith hero of the Centauromachy.
etymology: Ancient Greek Καινεύς (Kaineús); same name as the Lapith, but a later Coronid generation in Argonaut catalogues.

sections.heading: Coronid Argonaut
paragraphs: Hyginus (Fabulae 14) lists Caeneus son of Coronus from Gortyn among the Argonauts. Apollodorus (Bibliotheca 1.9.16) counts a Caeneus beside Coronus son of Caeneus — treating the Argonaut as a distinct entry. Wikipedia's Caeneus article is primarily the Lapith; its notes record the Hyginian "Caeneus son of Coronus" catalogue line, which under one reading makes this Argonaut a grandson of the Lapith.
The invulnerable Lapith — born Caenis, transformed by Poseidon, hammered into the earth by centaurs — is a different figure (atlas id caeneus-lapith).

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas keeps caeneus-gortyn (Argonaut from Gortyn) strictly apart from caeneus-lapith. Do not merge the two under the shared Wikipedia title.
